questions.question: What was GPT-4's accuracy on Game of 24 with chain-of-thought versus Tree of Thoughts?
questions.explanation: GPT-4 with chain-of-thought hit only 4% on Game of 24, while Tree of Thoughts (Yao et al., NeurIPS 2023) achieved 74% by enabling search with self-evaluation at each node.

questions.question: What does LATS unify under Monte Carlo Tree Search?
options: Tree of Thoughts, ReAct, and Reflexion
questions.explanation: LATS (Zhou et al., ICML 2024) unifies Tree of Thoughts (tree search with self-eval), ReAct (environment-grounded tool use), and Reflexion (failure-driven verbal reflection) under one MCTS framework.

questions.question: What are the four phases of MCTS per iteration in LATS?
questions.explanation: Each MCTS iteration in LATS runs: Select (walk the tree using UCT), Expand (generate K children via policy), Simulate (rollout and score with value function), Backpropagate (update visit counts and Q values up the path).

questions.question: What token cost does ToT impose on Game of 24 compared to chain-of-thought?
questions.explanation: Tree of Thoughts on Game of 24 uses 100-1000x the tokens of chain-of-thought. Search is expensive; it should be reserved for tasks where a single trajectory is demonstrably insufficient.

questions.question: What pass@1 accuracy did LATS achieve on HumanEval with GPT-4?
questions.explanation: LATS achieved 92.7% pass@1 on HumanEval with GPT-4 at paper time, which was state-of-the-art, by using MCTS with tests as the value function.

questions.question: What is the UCT formula used in LATS for node selection?
questions.explanation: UCT (upper confidence bound for trees) balances exploitation (Q(s,a)) with exploration (c * sqrt(ln N(s) / N(s,a))). The constant c controls the exploration-exploitation tradeoff.
